name: Dafydd Nanmor
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Dafydd Nanmor was a fifteenth-century Welsh poet, named from Nanmor near Beddgelert. He wrote love poems in the manner of Dafydd ap Gwilym and later found patrons in South Wales; the Dictionary of Welsh Biography calls him a poet of note but dates him only to the fifteenth century.
The poem here is George Borrow's English version, taken from his Wild Wales and printed in Welsh Poems and Ballads (1915).

poems.title: Ryce of Twyn
poems.author: Dafydd Nanmor
poems.note: From "Wild Wales"; the source attributes it to Dafydd Nanmor.
poems.translator: trans. George Borrow (Welsh Poems and Ballads, 1915)
poems.text:
FOR Ryce if hundred thousands plough'd,
The lands around his fair abode;
Did vines of thousand vineyards bleed,
Still corn and wine great Ryce would need;
If all the earth had bread's sweet savour,
And water all had cyder's flavour,
Three roaring feasts in Ryce's hall
Would swallow earth and ocean all.
